Please indicate: Yes, No, or Unknown. If yes, please specify. 7. In the past three weeks, have you been in any of the following situations: Were you exposed to the blood or other body fluids of a person with Ebola Virus Disease (EVD)? Yes, No, or Unknown. If yes, did you ever NOT wear waterproof gloves, gown, face mask, and/or goggles? Yes, No, or Unknown. Did you get pricked with a needle or other sharp object, or were you splashed in the eye, nose, or mouth? Yes, No, or Unknown. Did you provide direct care to a person with EVD while they were sick? Yes, No, or Unknown. If yes, did you ever NOT wear waterproof gloves, gown, face mask, and/or goggles? Yes, No, or Unknown. Did you work in a laboratory where body fluids of EVD patients were processed? Yes, No, or Unknown. If yes, did you ever NOT wear waterproof gloves, gown, face mask, and/or goggles? Yes, No, or Unknown. Did you directly handle dead bodies, such as participating in a funeral, burial rites, or other activities involving handling dead bodies? Yes, No, or Unknown. If yes, did you ever NOT wear waterproof gloves, gown, face mask, and/or goggles? Yes, No, or Unknown. Have you spent time in the same room as a person with EVD? Yes, No, or Unknown. If yes, did you ever NOT wear waterproof gloves, gown, face mask, and/or goggles? Yes, No, or Unknown. If yes, were you always at least 1 meter away from the person with EVD? Yes, No, or Unknown. If yes, did you spend a long period of time in the room (more than just walking past the area)? Yes, No, or Unknown. If yes, did you have any physical contact with the person with EVD, such as shaking hands or touching any body part? Yes, No, or Unknown. 8. Have you been interviewed as part of a contact-tracing investigation after an individual was confirmed to have EVD? Yes, No, or Unknown. 9. If you have been exposed to EVD and are experiencing symptoms consistent with the disease, public health officials require that you undergo medical evaluation. You will be taken to a hospital emergency department. At the hospital, a doctor will examine you. Based on the results of the examination, you may be tested for EVD if recommended by public health officials. Follow all instructions provided by public health and medical personnel to prevent exposing others. 10. If your medical evaluation does not indicate EVD infection: You will be allowed to leave the hospital. However, continue to take steps to protect yourself and others until 21 days after leaving the Ebola-affected country: Take your temperature every morning and evening, and monitor for symptoms consistent with Ebola, such as fever, severe headache, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, or unexplained bleeding and bruising. Check in regularly with public health officials as instructed. Inform public health officials if you plan to travel more than 50 miles or to another country. Do not travel on commercial planes, ships, or trains. 11. If you develop a fever of 38°C (100.4°F) or higher, or feel like you have a fever: Contact a public health official or call a doctor. Inform them of your travel history and potential exposure to Ebola. Do not use public transport to get to the medical facility. Travel only by private car or ambulance. Bring this notice and provide it to healthcare staff upon arrival. 12. For individuals who may have been exposed to EVD, further evaluation and monitoring are critical to ensure public safety and prevent the spread of the disease.
